measurement: Ask accuracy hill-climb on DBpedia 2022.12.01: predicate-use grounding, popularity-ordered linking and two generic prompt rules, against the main-branch baseline, with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5
host: A development laptop with 16 cores and 30 GB of memory that was running other work. Binaries were built on atlas and copied back.

scoring.headline: rdf-term-set-projected-columns-v2, the strict score of record
scoring.secondary: rdf-term-set-projected-guarded-lenient-v3 with gold-errata-v1, defined by testsuite/ask/eval_support/guarded.py at commit 65d648d3, with which every run below was rescored
scoring.unflagged: guarded passes minus those flagged predicate_column, predicate_column_unknown or projection_drops_rows

split.fresh: fresh-150, from the QALD-9-plus training split, 150 of 306 scorable questions chosen by SHA256 of "ask-hillclimb-fresh-v1:ID" after 6 duplicates of test or db25 questions were dropped

notes: Haiku QALD runs h-v3-qald-r1 and h-v3-qald-r2 used commit 30b0a968, which builds the same prompts on this database as 570d7062, as the dry runs show.
h-base-fresh-r1 stopped after 42 of 150 questions on five provider errors in a row; h-base-fresh-r1b is the full rerun.
The Sonnet and Opus QALD and db25 baselines are the 7b3b6df5 runs of the earlier paid record, rescored here.
db25-65, a comma-separated literal gold, stays wrong under both scores pending an owner decision.
